candidates.statement: The stakeholder hopes that his experience will help the interviewer get a deeper view of how users want to use this product.

evidence_candidates.quote: I hope my experience would help you get a deeper view of how user want to use this product.

candidates.statement: He uses email to get mail from recruiters while applying for jobs, and checks email every day so as not to lose new information.

evidence_candidates.quote: So one of the goals that I would use email currently is to get the email from recruiters. So I'm applying for jobs. And I would check my email every day to make sure that I I didn't lose any new information on that.

candidates.statement: A second goal is to check news and notifications broadcast by the school.

evidence_candidates.quote: And also my second my second goal would be to check about the news that broadcasted by school. This kind of notification.

candidates.statement: For personal purposes he uses email to book appointments at a dentist or clinic.

evidence_candidates.quote: For booking. I let's say, dentist or clinic or booking the appointment.

candidates.statement: He uses email to receive information from merchandise, such as sales or discounts.

evidence_candidates.quote: And also, I use email to get the information from merchandise, like, if they have sales or discounts, I'll get it from an email yeah

candidates.statement: He also (rarely) uses email to contact friends.

evidence_candidates.quote: But I also use email to contact with my friends.

candidates.statement: Typical daily flow: open the browser, open Gmail, scan unread mail, star what looks important, delete trash/spam, then read the important emails.

evidence_candidates.quote: So I think a typical flow that I use email is that, I open the browser. I get it into Gmail. And then I look at those mails that I haven't read, and I take a quick glance on every mail, and if that's something I think is important. I will 1st market. and then, if those are like trash or spam, I will just delete it. and then I will. Read those emails that that is important.

candidates.statement: If a reply leaves a task he cannot do now, he tags the email and returns to finish the task when available.

evidence_candidates.quote: And if there's some task I have to, I have to do after reply or something. But I couldn't do it now. I would just like tag it and then leave it there. and when I'm available I will check in and finish the task.

candidates.statement: To keep the inbox manageable he deletes mail that is not important, so the inbox is clearer.

evidence_candidates.quote: the tips I follow myself to make sure that my inbox is manageable is by as I, as I said, I would delete those mails that are not that important to make it more clear

candidates.statement: He also deletes important mails once the conversation has reached its end.

evidence_candidates.quote: and also even for the the important males. But if the conversation has reached to the end. I also did it.

candidates.statement: He keeps separate email accounts per purpose (recruiting, school notifications, special deals) so important mail stays distinguishable.

evidence_candidates.quote: I do this by have separate emails. So for some emails, it's really important like, I use it for recruiting.

candidates.statement: When writing or replying he first lists the main points (purpose, 2-3 sentences), asks an AI assistant tool to compose the email, then adjusts it a little.
candidates.modality: current practice with an external tool

evidence_candidates.quote: I would usually use AI assistant tool. Not necessarily in build assistant tool. So I would 1st list my main point.
And then I would ask the AI Assistant tool to compose an email for me. and I would adjust it a little bit

candidates.statement: He also adjusts the font size and bolds the important sentences before sending.

evidence_candidates.quote: Also adjust the font size and mark the marks. The sentence. mark the important sentence as bold, and then send it.

candidates.statement: When sending multimedia he uploads it to the cloud and sends the link, because he thinks the recipient can then view it on any platform.

evidence_candidates.quote: If I am sending multi media, I would probably upload it to the cloud and then send the link, because I think it's easier for the client to view it in any platform, including like Mobile or laptop.

candidates.statement: Automatic categorization sometimes puts important emails into the spam folder.

evidence_candidates.quote: sometimes there are some important emails that will like end up in the spans folder.

candidates.statement: He would rather receive some spam than miss important messages.

evidence_candidates.quote: because I would rather receive some spans instead of ignoring some important messages.

candidates.statement: With the current client a send can only be cancelled within 3 seconds after sending.

evidence_candidates.quote: And after you're sending an email, you could cancel the sending action in 3 seconds.

candidates.statement: It would be better to have a function for editing an already sent email instead of sending a new one, with the recipient seeing the new version and being able to view the edit history.

evidence_candidates.quote: It would probably be better if there's an function of editing the email instead of sending a new one. So for the client. They could see the new email and old email, but they will see the new one. And if they want, they could see the editing history.

candidates.statement: Security is not a personal concern because he does not send confidential messages by email.

evidence_candidates.quote: because I don't send confidential messages through email.

candidates.statement: Reliability problem: some emails that should arrive (for example website sign-up mail) sometimes never reach the inbox.

evidence_candidates.quote: the issue of about reliabilities for me is that sometimes I would not receive some emails like I'm not sure if you have this experience. But when you register some website and then send email to your inbox, and for some reason they're just not there.

candidates.statement: The missing-email problem is quite an obstacle for him.

evidence_candidates.quote: And yeah, I think that's something that is quite an obstacle for me.

candidates.statement: Ideal scenario: he types two terse lines to a professor and the assistant composes a well-organized email for him.
context: AI assistance built into the email

evidence_candidates.quote: the ideal scenario would be if I just type. Dear Professor, what does the requirement for homework? One. Do we have to do? A or B, and it will just like compose and more like, well organized email for me.

candidates.statement: He praises the existing warning that appears before sending when the mail refers to a resume that was not attached.
candidates.modality: positive evaluation of an existing feature

evidence_candidates.quote: But I didn't attach the resume. It will warn me before I send it. I think that is really good.

candidates.statement: He starts to propose another feature about what happens when he receives an email (sentence left unfinished).

evidence_candidates.quote: I also think about another like feature. That would be good.

candidates.statement: It would also be good if the AI assistant could get the main point of a received email.

evidence_candidates.quote: If AI assistant could help me. Get the main point of that email.

candidates.statement: The assistant highlights keywords in the email.

evidence_candidates.quote: And this highlights the keywords something like the.

candidates.statement: With highlighting he would not miss keywords; a TikTok assessment mail buried a small line saying the test should not be taken twice, and he lost time because of it.

evidence_candidates.quote: Yeah, and then I won't miss missed out some keywords.
I saw there's a small line on in the email saying, like you, we don't recommend you to take this twice like the second time.

candidates.statement: He uses the client at least 5 times a day because he does not want to miss any message from the recruiting team.

evidence_candidates.quote: So currently, cause I don't want to miss any message recruiting team. So I used at least 5 times a day.

candidates.statement: The actual usage frequency is 10 to 20 times a day.

evidence_candidates.quote: 10 to 20, yeah.

candidates.statement: The routine task that could be simplified is reading all the emails; an AI assistant for that would be very helpful because he spends a lot of time reading every email.
candidates.modality: improvement wish ('could be simplified', 'would be very helpful')

evidence_candidates.quote: the routing test, I think, could be simplified is by reading all the emails.
if we have, I assistant for that, that would be very helpful, because I spend a lot of time just reading every email.

candidates.statement: The interviewer proposes a periodic digest (3 emails instead of 30); the stakeholder answers only that it could be one solution.

evidence_candidates.quote: maybe you just get 3 emails instead of 30 emails.
Yeah, that that could be one solution. Yeah.

candidates.statement: It would be good to get notifications for important messages, but current clients cannot identify important mail well, so he would not rely on that unless it is really reliable and prefers not to rely fully on AI.
context: only if importance detection is really reliable

evidence_candidates.quote: it would be good to receive notification for some important messages. But I think the point is that for current application. There is no a very good way to identify important messages from the others.
I would probably not want to rely on that. Unless it's really reliable.

candidates.statement: Crashing or lagging happens very rarely; he is happy with current reliability.

evidence_candidates.quote: Crashing or lagging. Very, very few. I don't really remember a time.

candidates.statement: Existing features such as forwarding and BCC to everyone in his group are important for working under deadline.

evidence_candidates.quote: I think the existing features. Including the function of forwarding the email. And BBC, like, sent to all the people in my group.

candidates.statement: Those team-wide sending features would be very important when working on deadlines.

evidence_candidates.quote: That would be very important when it comes to working on deadlines.

candidates.statement: Searching is the most important feature and is used every day; tag filtering could be done by searching, so scheduling ranks second.

evidence_candidates.quote: the most important would definitely be searching. That's really important. I use it every day, and filtering by tags, or like I would say it's it could be done by searching, so I would say the second one will probably be scheduling.

candidates.statement: Future need: embed an AI assistant that helps read and write emails.

evidence_candidates.quote: as I mentioned we could embed, embed some AI assistant to help us read and write emails.

candidates.statement: He introduces a second future idea while conceding it is probably not that practical.

evidence_candidates.quote: And second, I would say. it's probably not that practical, but.

candidates.statement: Category/protocol emails: a user self-assigns a category id (for example recruiting notifications for HR) and people who set the same id can communicate through that category.
context: stakeholder says it is probably not that practical

evidence_candidates.quote: we could have different category or protocol emails. So for example, if I didn't, if I self identify a category that say, given an id for 8,000, and if my friend also set up this like 8,000 in his app, then we could communicate through like we could identify self, identify the category
I could set a tag categories for recruiting notifications for Hr.

candidates.statement: Future use would be mostly at work.

evidence_candidates.quote: I would say, mostly at work.

candidates.statement: Future use would be professional communication with people, not necessarily inside his own company.

evidence_candidates.quote: So I would say, mostly connected to people like, not necessarily people in my company, but just like, professionally, yeah.
